title: The Wax Lion in the Iron Cage (TE)
summary: A foreign emperor sends an iron cage containing a fierce lion without a door or latch. Birbal removes the lion using heat and science. [TE]
full_text:
A foreign monarch sent an extraordinary challenge to Emperor Akbar at Agra. An emissary wheeled a heavy cart into the center of the Diwan-i-Khas, bearing a colossal, seamless iron cage. Inside paced a fierce, golden-maned lion with bared fangs, looking terrifyingly lifelike.

The emissary read the challenge: 'We challenge the counselors of Akbar to remove this fierce lion from this cage. But heed these two conditions: the iron bars must not be bent, sawed, or damaged, and the cage possesses neither a door, a keyhole, nor a sliding latch! If you fail within twenty-four hours, your court must admit defeat.'

The ministers inspected the cage. The iron bars were thick, seamless, and welded together without a single opening large enough for a kitten to squeeze through. Several nobles tried prying the bars with levers, but the solid iron did not budge.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can you free this beast without damaging the cage?'

Birbal walked slowly around the cage, studying the lion's golden coat, rigid posture, and unblinking glass eyes. He noticed a faint sheen on the lion's flank where a warm sunbeam fell through the arched window.

Birbal smiled gently: 'Sire, I shall remove the lion before this assembly within an hour.'

Birbal instructed an attendant to bring a brazier of glowing red coals and a long iron rod. Birbal thrust the rod into the embers until the tip glowed bright crimson.

Walking to the cage, Birbal slipped the glowing iron rod between the bars and gently pressed the tip against the lion's shoulder.

*Sssssss!*

A fragrant plume of melted beeswax and honey scented the entire chamber! The flank of the lion softened and began to drip into the tray below!

Birbal pressed the hot rod against the neck, head, and paws. Within thirty minutes, the entire 'lion'—which was expertly sculpted from solid beeswax painted with golden ochre—melted completely away, flowing out between the iron bars as a pool of warm liquid wax, leaving the iron cage completely empty and entirely undamaged!

The court erupted in thunderous applause. The foreign emissary bowed in awe: 'Emperor Akbar, your minister sees through every illusion.'

Akbar rewarded Birbal with a jeweled dagger, reminding everyone that problems that appear terrifying on the outside often dissolve when inspected with calm reason.
